description.ncbi_summary: This gene is one of two arylamine N-acetyltransferase (NAT) genes in the human genome, and is orthologous to the mouse and rat Nat2 genes. The enzyme encoded by this gene catalyzes the transfer of an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to various arylamine and hydrazine substrates. This enzyme helps metabolize drugs and other xenobiotics, and functions in folate catabolism. Multiple transcript variants encoding different isoforms have been found for this gene. [provided by RefSeq, Aug 2011].

uniprot_function.text: Xenobiotic-metabolizing enzyme that catalyzes both N-acetylation (usually detoxification) and O-acetylation (usually bioactivation) of a wide range of species-specific substrates including hydrazines, aromatic amine drugs and aromatic amine carcinogens (Probable) (PubMed:9168895). Transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-coenzyme A to arylamine and N-hydroxyarylamine acceptor substrates (Probable) (PubMed:9168895). Can also transfer an N-acetyl group from an N-hydroxy acetylamine to either N-hydroxyarylamine or arylamine in the absence of acetyl-coenzyme A (PubMed:9168895). Therefore, activates N-hydroxyarylamines to unstable acetoxy intermediates which decompose to electrophiles, bind to DNA, and lead to mutagenesis and carcinogenesis (PubMed:9168895). Plays a significant role in the bioactivation and detoxification of many drugs and carcinogens (Probable) (PubMed:9168895).
